about: Statements by others (the operator, institutions, studies) and how far they are tested. Status vocabulary: supported, published (one study, not replicated), pending (test planned), tension (contradicts another statement), unverifiable (as stated), contradicted.

claims.text: Costs of up to EUR 350,000 a year, partly financed by the Province of Trento.
claims.test: Provincial acts, civic access request, right of reply.

claims.text: 2010 cover of 76,400 m2; about 52% less ablation.
claims.test: Single season, one station per surface.

claims.text: Up to 69% less melt; albedo about 50% higher than ice.
claims.test: Single season.

claims.text: Used sheets reused as the installation The Invisible Mountain.
claims.test: Betti and Fleck (2021): a 5 x 15 m piece shown in Venice; sheets used two seasons, then about 17 t a year sent to the Bolzano waste-to-energy plant. Ask operator and plant for records.

claims.text: About 0.18 km2 of glacier covered in Switzerland; up to 350,000 m3 of ice saved a year.
claims.test: Context and scale only.

claims.text: The Presena glacier is a Site of Community Importance.
claims.test: Current Natura 2000 status; candidate site IT3120158.

claims.text: Covers reduce melt by about 50%.
claims.test: Consistent with C02 and C03 (published field measurements).

claims.text: Covered areas absorb 36% of solar energy, uncovered areas 57%.
claims.who: Operator, attributed to University of Milan
claims.test: Confirmed by AINEVA Neve e Valanghe 74: albedo 0.64 on the cover vs 0.43 on the glacier, 31 Jul-29 Aug 2010; absorbed 36% vs 57%.

claims.text: After six seasons the covers preserved 2.5 m of snow; uncovered ice dropped 11 m.
claims.test: AINEVA documents a step of about 1.5-2 m after the single summer 2010: 11 m in six seasons is plausible in order of magnitude. Still to measure with LiDAR 2006-09 vs 2014/2018.

Sentinel-2, preliminary, not validated (v3.5, 23 Nov 2026). The cover is visible every summer 2016-2026. Visible area (lower-upper, m2): 2016 26,000-59,000 vs claim 50,000 (within range); 2017 27,000-52,000 vs 65,000; 2019 9,000-53,000 vs 100,000; 2020 5,000-88,000 vs 110,000; 2021 31,000-102,000 vs 110,000. Earlier runs (16 Nov) gave lower values; results changed as cloud, shadow, rock and snow errors were fixed. Possible reasons for the gap: fabric vs visible area, sheets under snow or in shadow, covers outside the zone. Also in tension with C02. Documented areas before: 28,000 (2008), 37,300 (2009), 76,400 (2010; about 70,000 in the 2013 thesis), 57,800 (2011).

claims.text: Partly financed by the Province, and carried out 'in total autonomy'.
claims.test: AINEVA: an experimental programme approved by the Province and a convention between the Province and the lift company; the 2012 thesis says covers were laid by the lift company and the Province. Funding share still unknown; provincial acts and right of reply.

claims.text: 350,000 m2 of snow laid every winter; yearly loss of 600,000 m2 of ice mass.
claims.test: Units mix area and volume; ask the operator.

claims.text: Strips of 5 x 70 m, 500 g/m2, 4 mm thick, EUR 2/m2; more than 300 sheets.
claims.test: AINEVA and Betti and Fleck give TOPTEX GLS 340 (340 g/m2, made in Linz), and the 2012 thesis names TenCate Toptex GLS 340; the 2010 thesis section and the operator give 500 g/m2. Possibly different fabrics in different years.

claims.text: A covered glacier will never disappear: it stays as a rectangular mass kept with snowmaking (2021 MUSE study).
claims.test: Find the MUSE study itself.

claims.text: Covers 2008-2011: 28,000, 37,300, 76,400 and 57,800 m2, with maps for each year.
claims.who: Diolaiuti et al., AINEVA Neve e Valanghe 74 (with the Province of Trento)
claims.test: Compare 2010 with the 2013 thesis (about 70,000 m2); check maps against orthophotos.

claims.text: White geotextiles were already laid at the end of the 1990s on the right-hand side, after straw mulching and moved or artificial snow.
claims.test: Find photos or records of the 1990s covers.

claims.text: Every year 34 t of plastic cover the mountain; 17 t a year go as special waste to the Bolzano waste-to-energy plant.
claims.who: Betti and Fleck 2021 (materials from the operator)
claims.test: 34 t matches 100,000 m2 x 340 g/m2 (calculated). Ask the operator and the plant for disposal records.

claims.text: Covers are laid every year between May and June.
claims.test: 2010 laid 28 June (thesis); 2012 experiments from early July. Earlier laying since? Check with webcams and Sentinel-2 calendar (H3).

claims.text: Presena has the largest covered glacier surface in the world.
claims.test: No global inventory of covered glaciers; Austrian ski glaciers report over 100 ha in total.

claims.text: The Presena glacier has lost more than a third of its volume since 1993.
claims.test: Area series 82 ha (1961), 68 (1987), 33 (2003), 26 (2011) is documented by AINEVA; volume needs DEMs.
